basis: Acute myeloid leukemia is a malignant disease of myeloid blood cells and bone marrow.
Chronic inflammation of labial salivary glands and lip vermilion; unknown cause does not establish an immune mechanism. Associated carcinoma is a separate disease.
BCR-ABL1-positive acute myeloid leukemia affects myeloid blood cells and bone marrow.
Carcinoma arising from renal tubular epithelium; no additional metastatic organ consistently meets the 30% threshold across patients.
Benign mesothelial neoplasm confined to the fallopian tube, a reproductive organ outside the axes.
Defining skeletal malformations, anal atresia and urethral obstruction establish all three axes; autoimmune thrombocytopenia has no documented frequency.
Neurodevelopmental disorder defined by impaired acquisition and execution of coordinated motor skills.
BH4 recycling disorder causing hyperphenylalaninemia; developmental delay occurs in 5-29%. Frequent oculogyric crises alone do not establish lasting neurologic damage.
Carcinoma originating in the tongue and oral cavity.
Colonic aganglionosis and peripheral neuroblastic tumors define the syndrome. Arrhythmia/QT abnormalities have 80-99% HPO frequency, despite occasional dysautonomia in the definition.
Renal salt-wasting tubulopathy defined by hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis; hearing loss is restricted to particular subtypes.
Defined by congenital cardiac malformations, conduction disease and cardiomyopathy; myopathy here is cardiac.
Inherited sickling hemoglobinopathy with beta-plus thalassemia; severity varies, and additional organ damage is not established in at least 30% across this subtype.
Cerebellar malformation and developmental delay define Joubert syndrome. Pituitary abnormalities/low IGF-1 occur in 2/2; strabismus and hypermetropia in 1/2 reported patients.
Purine metabolism disorder; stones occur in 1/5 and renal insufficiency in 5-29%. Myalgia in 2/5 does not establish muscle damage.
Metabolic steatotic liver disease defined by hepatic fat accumulation and metabolic dysfunction; associated diabetes and cardiovascular disease are separately diagnosed conditions.
CRYBB2-related cataract is a disease of the ocular lens.
Skeletal dysplasia with defining Pelger-Huet neutrophil nuclear abnormalities, documented in 2/2; no evidence of associated immune dysfunction.
Familial benign setting-sun phenomenon is an ocular position/gaze abnormality; no underlying neurologic disease is established by this concept.
Defined by pulmonary fibrosis and/or marrow failure. Cirrhosis occurs in 3/134 and osteopenia in 35/134, below 30%; premature graying does not establish skin damage.
Congenital fistula directly connects the esophagus and trachea; recurrent aspiration-related infections do not make this an infectious disease.
MAGED2-related renal salt-wasting tubulopathy with defining electrolyte disturbances; the transient course does not change its primary organ classification.
Myelodysplasia, immunodeficiency and psychomotor developmental delay are defining components; short stature and facial dysmorphism alone do not establish skeletal damage.
Structural disease of the subclavian artery; stroke and limb ischemia are potential complications without evidence of a frequency of at least 30%.
Mature T-cell lymphoma involving lymphoid tissue and often marrow/spleen. Rash alone does not establish damaging skin infiltration; other organ damage lacks a clear 30% frequency.
